title: IT / Finance / Security Ops Sync
topics: KMS / key rotation and encryption in transit
Billing anomalies and Dedicated capacity budget
Log retention / audit logs and retention policy
summary: Weekly ops sync between IT, Finance and Security. Main outcomes: firm SOC 2 audit timeline (end of Q4), action to update KMS runbook, finance to confirm reserved capacity budget, and security to share audit evidence checklist. Agreed next checkpoints and owners.
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: ok starting now, thanks everyone for jumping on. um this is the weekly it/finance/security ops sync, 45 minutes on the calendar.
[00:12] Erin: hey, hi, everyone. I have the SOC 2 timeline notes open — quick heads up, auditor availability tightened up for November.
[00:25] Maya: okay, November is tight, but finance windows look ok as long as we commit by mid-September on the budget, right Samir?
[00:36] Samir: yeah that's the ask. we need to lock the reserved capacity commit for Dedicated by sept 17 to hit Q4 provisioning. if we miss that it pushes costs up.
[00:49] Jordan: from an ops perspective the infra lead time for GPUs is roughly 6–8 weeks once we sign. but we also have some headroom with cloud bursts.
[00:59] Diego: legal side — procurement docs are almost done, Diego here — we need the final SOW and the enterprise terms. Samir, can you share the draft?
[01:12] Samir: yep I'll share the SOW draft after the call, will put link in slack (link: drive/redwood/procurement/sow_draft_v2.docx).
[01:24] Erin: on SOC 2: I ran a quick gap analysis. main items outstanding: KMS key rotation proof, audit log retention policy (90 vs 365 days), and sampling of change control tickets.
[01:37] Hannah: about logs, we're still shipping logs to the central ELK for 90 days — extending to 365 is possible but storage cost jumps.
[01:48] Maya: can you quantify cost delta? we need that to make the finance case.
[01:53] Hannah: rough ballpark, maybe 18k a month extra — again depends on retention tier and compression. I'll get a spreadsheet.
[02:03] Samir: okay please attach a line-item to the budget ask. also there's been a pattern of weird charges in last month's billing — some burst credits didn't apply — I uploaded a spreadsheet (link: drive/redwood/billing/sep_anomalies.xlsx).
[02:16] Maya: I saw that. looks like a reconciliation mismatch across regions. I'll follow up with cloud billing support but would like ops to confirm tagging is consistent.
[02:28] Jordan: tagging: yes, we've got a couple of orphaned instances that slipped through due to a deploy script bug. I can run a tagging sweep this week.
[02:39] Erin: back to KMS — do we have enterprise KMS integrated for Dedicated? I thought we had a hybrid mode?
[02:46] Jordan: currently Dedicated supports customer-managed keys via KMS (we call it KMS-keywrap), but the runbook is incomplete for rotate/rollover. sometimes KMS is verbalized as K-M-S in notes, sorry the transcript tools butcher acronyms.
[02:59] Diego: from compliance: we need documented rotation schedule and proof of rotation in the audit window. is that automated?
[03:07] Jordan: rotation is automated for cloud-managed keys but for customer-managed keys it's manual unless you wire an automation — we can add a lambda to rotate and push to audit log.
[03:16] Erin: okay add automation to action items, need evidence in the control matrix. also we need to capture who has access to key material — RBAC list.
[03:25] Samir: do we have a current RBAC export?
[03:28] Hannah: yes, I generated an export last week — it's in the security repo (link: git.redwood/security/rbac_export_2025-09-03.csv) but I need to scrub a couple of service accounts.
[03:40] Maya: on procurement timing — if we commit to Dedicated, what's the discount shape? Samir?
[03:45] Samir: typical committed discount tiers are 30/50/70 depending on duration and GPU type. I'll push a pricing sheet after we confirm resource profile.
[03:56] Maya: resource profile — we run a batch of embedding jobs nightly and have interactive chat traffic during business hours. can we get a throughput/latency estimate?
[04:07] Jordan: yes, preliminary numbers: with the configured pooling and batching we expect median p95 latencies around 220–300ms for short prompts, throughput ~80 requests/sec for embeddings when batch size is tuned. that's based on current model weights — can re-run with new model quantization.
[04:25] Erin: also log retention affects forensic capability for any data incidents; if we only keep 90 days and the incident windows spans beyond, auditors will flag it.
[04:37] Diego: legal wants to see the incident runbook and evidence of post-incident review — do we have an up-to-date runbook?
[04:44] Hannah: the incident runbook was updated in July — I can link it, but need to add steps for KMS compromise and cross-region failover.
[04:55] Samir: ok action: Hannah update runbook with KMS compromise play and cross-region failover.
[05:00] [05:00] Erin: and Erin will circulate SOC 2 evidence checklist.
[05:05] Erin: yes I'll put the checklist in the shared folder (link: drive/redwood/security/soc2_checklist_v3.pdf) and tag the controls we need owners for.
[05:14] Maya: for the budget, I need two numbers — incremental monthly cost for 365-day logs, and the committed capacity monthly payment options (12 vs 24 months).
[05:25] Samir: I'll get both lines in the deck.
[05:28] Jordan: quick note on telemetry: we should enable prefix caching metrics and kv cache hit rates for the model infra — that feeds the cost optimization piece.
[05:37] Maya: yeah the optimize recommendations depend on those stats. Samir, can you include model cache metrics in the cost deck?
[05:44] Samir: yep I'll pull the metrics and include a slide.
[05:49] [10:00] — (larger discussion on audit-specific evidence) —
[10:05] Erin: auditors tend to want at least 3 months of logs as immediate evidence but they'll want historical context; we should plan to provide longer retention as compensating control if we can't keep everything for 365 days.
[10:20] Diego: what if we use tiered retention — 90 days on hot ELK, archive to S3 with immutability for 365+? that would lower monthly costs.
[10:30] Hannah: yes we can lifecycle to S3 glacier and keep indexed pointers for search, cost-effective. I'll draft a retention architecture doc.
[10:40] Maya: good, include cost delta in the doc.
[10:43] Samir: note: open billing anomaly — there was an unusual egress charge in eu-west-1. Jordan, can you validate the traffic patterns?
[10:51] Jordan: will do, will check VPC flow logs and cross-check service-to-service egress. might be a backup job that ran in the wrong region.
[11:01] Erin: for SOC 2 evidence we'll need to sign-off owners — control owners list needs to be finalized.
[11:07] Samir: I'll draft initial owners and share.
[11:11] Maya: also need to confirm invoice treatment for committed capacity — capital vs operating? our accounting will need guidance.
[11:18] Diego: legal to check contract language for term length and early termination fees.
[11:23] Samir: ok let's go around with final quick calls — any blockers?
[11:27] Jordan: none besides the tagging sweep and runbook updates.
[11:30] Hannah: I'll start the retention architecture doc and tagging sweep.
[11:33] Erin: I'll circulate the SOC 2 checklist and control owners.
[11:36] Maya: I'll confirm budget numbers and follow up on billing anomaly with cloud support.
[11:42] Samir: great — recap next steps and owners — we'll meet same time next week. thanks everyone.
[11:49] (end)

Jordan to run tagging sweep and validate VPC flow logs, report by 2025-09-14
Hannah to draft retention architecture and update incident runbook by 2025-09-15

Samir to share SOW/pricing sheet and billing anomalies spreadsheet after call
